thread.title: Tech stocks poised to book another record, but broader market set for muted action

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Tech stocks poised to book another record, but broader market set for muted action
text:
U.S. stock-index futures were trading at break-even levels Tuesday, but the technology-laden Nasdaq was set to notch a second straight record after marking its first all-time high since mid March in the previous session, underscoring a resurgence in the sector that has been among the market’s more influential.
What are markets doing? Dow Jones Industrial Average futures YMM8, +0.02% were down 4 points, or less than 0.1%, to 24,791, while S&P 500 index futures ESM8, +0.05% was little changed at 2,745.25. Nasdaq-100 futures NQM8, +0.16% gained 6.75 points, or 0.1%, to 7,155.
On Monday, the Nasdaq Composite COMP, +0.21% closed at a record for the first time since March 12, rising 0.7%, to 7,606.46. The S&P 500 SPX, +0.03% finished 0.5%, to 2,746.87, while, the Dow DJIA, -0.03% advanced 178.48 points, or 0.7%, to 24,813.69.
Read: Techs lead buyback boom, on track to put trillions back into investor hands
The small-capitalization oriented Russell 2000 index RUT, +0.33% also closed at a fresh all-time peak, rising 0.3%, to 1,653.37.
What was driving the market? Investors were hunting for fresh catalysts to keep the start-of-the-week gains for stocks going, as they regroup after recent market upheaval triggered by political stress in Italy. More stability on that front could be coming, if the new Italian coalition government makes it past a confidence vote in parliament.
Some inspiration may come from the technology sector, given the gains for the Nasdaq. Apple Inc. shares were higher in premarket trading, after scoring a record finish on Monday, as details from its software-focused Worldwide Developers Conference emerged. A rise for Twitter shares was also playing its part. In Tuesday trade, European tech stocks SX8R, +2.03% hit a 17-year high, according to FactSet.
Investors appeared to be putting trade tensions aside, even after trade talks broke down between the U.S. and China over the weekend. But leaders of the Group of Seven nations will hold talks in Canada on Friday and Saturday, where tariffs and trade are likely to be discussed. This weekend’s rebuke by G-7 finance ministers of the Trump administration’s trade tariffs could add some stress to the gathering.
Read: Death knell for the G-7 may be at hand after hostile reaction to Trump tariffs
What are strategists saying? “So far, investors remain focused on a broader subset of U.S. economic data, while concluding that U.S. earnings and the economy are sufficiently robust to keep the equity bull market intact. And for now, putting the prospects of higher U.S. interest rates and global trade wars, which usually scare investors stiff, on the back burner,” said Stephen Innes, senior trader with OANDA.
“Momentum buying is behind the markets climb being led the good macro and tech news. Investors are placing aside trade worries for now, as the healthy state of the economy overrules,” said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities, in emailed comments.
Which stocks were in focus? Mylan NV MYL, +6.21% shares surged nearly 5% in premarket after the drugmaker received Food and Drug Administration approval for a drug similar to one made by Amgen Inc. AMGN, -1.22%
Twitter Inc. TWTR, +4.12% shares jumped over 5% in premarket trading after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the microblogging platform’s stock would join the S&P 500 index .
Shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.69% rose 0.6% in premarket. Among the company’s WWDC announcements were new augmented-reality development tools and software upgrades for all its products, along with a new Apple Watch.
See: Apple’s WWDC: Blocks on Facebook sharing s urprise, but no lift to $1 trillion market cap
Starbucks Corp. SBUX, -2.16% slipped 1.4% in premarket trading after its executive chairman, Howard Schultz, said he would step down late Monday .
What’s on the economic calendar? The Markit services purchasing managers index for May will be released at 9:45 a.m. Eastern Time, following by the ISM’s services index for May and job openings for April at 10 a.m.
Opinion: A new economic indicator is saying there is no sign of a U.S. recession
See: MarketWatch’s economic calendar
What are other markets doing? Asian stocks finished mostly higher , while the Stoxx Europe 600 index SXXP, +0.19% climbed as the tech sector hit a 17-year high .
Crude oil CLN8, -0.59% reversed direction, falling 0.5% to $64.40 a barrel, after settling at the lowest level in nearly two months on Monday. Gold GCQ8, -0.02% drifted lower at $1,294.80 an ounce, while the ICE U.S. Dollar Index DXY, +0.12% was also steady at 94.039.
Barbara Kollmeyer Barbara Kollmeyer is an editor for MarketWatch in Madrid. Follow her on Twitter @bkollmeyer.
